verdicts.reasoning: Real, reproduced exactly (covered 5s countdown: done=0, isRunning=true, elapsed=1s until the page came back; covered stopwatch came back at 00:32.01; TickerMode off for 5s gave 00:06.10). Decision: keep time, and correct the doc, instead of pausing. Reasons: a muted Ticker keeps its clock (Flutter documents "time still elapses"), so the timer already came back with the covered time added, and pausing under a page while still running on through other spells without frames would have been the inconsistent choice; only keeping time removes the harm named in the finding (alarm fires late); and a caller who wants a pause can stop the timer through its controller, while nothing could give wall-clock time back to a pausing timer. Implementation: the state reads TickerMode.valuesOf in didChangeDependencies; while a running timer's ticker is muted, a 100ms periodic Timer counts in its place, so a countdown runs out there (onDone and the controller within about 0.1s) and elapsed and stop() are right to 0.1s. Beats do not repaint. When the ticker is audible again its own clock takes over, exact to the frame; a tick at elapsed zero means the ticker's clock only starts now (started between frames while muted), and what the beats counted is banked. A plain Stopwatch was not used because fake time in widget tests cannot drive it.

problems.title: Two dashed sides of different colours paint over each other in the corner they share

A translucent colour is blended twice there, and with opaque colours the corner takes the colour of whichever path is drawn last, which depends on the order the colours were first seen, not on the side. problems.title: A list that is being animated to another offset stops at its new end when rows go
problems.explanation:
`_KkScrollPhysics.adjustPositionForNewDimensions` clamps the offset even while an animation is moving the view. The framework's driven activity (`animateTo`, `ensureVisible` with a duration, the Page Up/Down and arrow-key `ScrollAction`, a tap on the scrollbar track) is not told about the clamp. On its next tick it asks for its own value, which now lies past the new end; the position reports overscroll and the activity ends. The list rests at the new end instead of the animation's target, and the future from `animateTo` completes as if it had arrived.

The usual case is an app that applies a filter and sends the list back to the top with `animateTo(0)`: the list ends at the bottom of the filtered rows. Before the fix, and with the physics the reviewer suggested, the animation reaches its target (showing space past the end on the way). A `KkScroll` has always behaved like the new code, because the framework's single-child viewport clamps too, so lists now match it. For lists it is a regression, and neither the report nor any test mentions animations.
problems.evidence:
Throwaway test (linux, harness): a 200px view with 20 rows of 50px at offset 800; `controller.animateTo(0, duration: 300ms, curve: KkSteps(6))`; in the same frame the list is pumped with 8 rows (max 200); then 40 frames of 16ms.
  Expected: <0>
    Actual: <200.0>
(`isScrollingNotifier.value` is already false.) The same test passes against the pre-fix scroll.dart and conveniences.dart.

Offsets every 50ms with `Curves.linear`:
- new code: 200, 200, 200, 200 ... (animateTo future completed)
- pre-fix code and `ClampingScrollPhysics(parent: RangeMaintainingScrollPhysics())`: 800, 667, 533, 400, 267, 133, 0

Rows removed 100ms into a 400ms animation (offset 600 at that moment): new code stays at 200; pre-fix code goes 600, 500, 400, 300, 200, 100, 0.
The same scenario with a KkScroll (child 1000 to 400): 200 before and after the fix.
problems.suggestedFix:
Decide the behaviour and pin it with a test. A physics object cannot tell an animation from a fling: both report `isScrolling` with a velocity, and a stepped curve reports velocity 0 between steps, like a resting finger. So the realistic choices are:
1. Keep the clamp, and say in the doc comment of `_KkScrollPhysics` (and of KkListView) that an animation in flight is dropped when the content gets shorter than where the view is, as a KkScroll has always done; apps should jump, or start the animation after the frame.
2. Do not clamp while the view moves toward the new range (`isScrolling`, velocity pointing into the range), and accept that a stepped animation between two steps is still cut and that an inward fling springs to the end.
3. Handle it above the physics, with a scroll position of KEIKAI's own that restarts the animation from the clamped offset.

problems.title: On touch platforms the scrollbar of every view now takes touches: a resting finger pages the view, a swipe over the thumb scrolls backwards
problems.explanation:
With `primary ?? false` and `_KkOwnScrollbar`, every plain KkScroll and KkListView has a working RawScrollbar on Android, iOS and Fuchsia. `KkScrollbar` leaves `RawScrollbar.interactive` at its default, which is true for every pointer kind. While the thumb shows (during a scroll and for 0.9s after), the bar therefore takes touches:
- A touch within 24px of the bar's centre line, anywhere along the track, that rests for 100ms counts as a tap on the track. The view pages by 80% of its height, with the framework's eased 100ms animation, also with motion off.
- A slow swipe that starts over the thumb drags the thumb, so the content runs the opposite way at the thumb's ratio.

Before the fix this was reachable only for a view with a controller of its own or the single primary view of a route. On a KkScreen with nav and body (the shared controller) the bar had no gestures, and in release no thumb. Flutter's own ScrollBehavior adds no scrollbar on touch platforms, Material's is not interactive on Android, and a browser's overlay scrollbar, which the design system relies on (`overflow: auto`), does not take touches. problems.title: A fling cut by the clamp ends inside layout: a listener that rebuilds on scroll end throws 'Build scheduled during frame'
problems.explanation:
Because the clamp also runs while the list is in a fling, the framework ends the fling from inside the viewport's `performLayout` (`applyNewDimensions`, then `goBallistic`, then `goIdle`). `ScrollEndNotification`, `UserScrollNotification` and `isScrollingNotifier` then fire in the layout phase. The framework's own listeners cope, and KEIKAI has none that rebuild. An app's usual `NotificationListener<ScrollEndNotification>` with `setState` does not: in debug it throws 'Build scheduled during frame.', which aborts `beginActivity`, so the position stays 'scrolling' for a frame and a second ScrollEndNotification follows. In release the rebuild is silently put off until something else asks for a frame.

Before the fix, and with the suggested RangeMaintaining physics, the end of this fling came from a ticker and such a listener was safe. Stock Flutter can end a fling inside layout in rarer cases, so this is an inherited hazard that the fix makes certain for 'rows go under a fling'. The fix's own test pins that path as wanted.
problems.evidence:
Throwaway test (android, harness): a KkListView of 40 rows under `NotificationListener<ScrollEndNotification>(onNotification: (n) { setState(() => ends++); return false; })`; fling by 3000px/s, 50ms later the list is pumped with 6 rows.
  Expected: null
    Actual: FlutterError:<Build scheduled during frame.
After that frame: offset 100, ends=1, isScrolling still true; next frame ends=2. The same test passes against the pre-fix files (ends=1, no error), and with `ClampingScrollPhysics(parent: RangeMaintainingScrollPhysics())`.

Notifications in the frame of the change, with the scheduler phase:
- new: ScrollEndNotification@100[persistentCallbacks], isScrolling=false[persistentCallbacks], UserScrollNotification@100[persistentCallbacks], Metrics@100[idle]
- pre-fix: Metrics@445[idle], then updates in transientCallbacks.
problems.suggestedFix: Let the fling end on the next tick instead of inside layout. One way, not tried here: `_KkScrollPhysics.createBallisticSimulation` returns a simulation that is already done when the position sits on an end with the velocity pointing outward, so the activity is replaced during layout and goes idle from the ticker. Otherwise say in the doc comment of the physics that a scroll can end during layout and listeners must not rebuild synchronously.

problems.title: Fix 201: a collapsed body is muted, not paused. Entrances in it run out unseen and never play when the panel opens; a value that changed while hidden is shown stale for one frame
problems.explanation:
`Visibility(visible: !collapsed, maintainState: true)` puts the body under `TickerMode(enabled: false)`. A muted Flutter ticker keeps its clock and only skips its callbacks, so the comment on lines 256-258 ("its animations rest") is wrong: every one-shot in the body is over by the time the body is shown.

- **Starts collapsed:** the entrance of whatever is in the body (the boot wipe of a readout, chart or timer, bar growth, needle sweep, scramble) is never seen. On the first frame after expanding it is at its start state (clip width 0, i.e. blank), and one frame later it is at its end.
- **Later expands:** only the body's own flicker replays.
- **Before the fix:** the entrances played on every expand, because the subtree was rebuilt.
- **Design source:** the stylesheet hides the body with `display: none` (bundle.css line 269). CSS restarts the animations of an element and its descendants when it gets a box again. So on the web each expand replays the body flicker and the `kk-boot` / `kk-grow` / `kk-needle` animations of everything in it (bundle.css lines 1916-1937), while state is kept. The README motion table lists these entrances as the motion of panels and charts.
- **Stale frame:** a ticker-driven value that changed while hidden is painted with its old value on the frame the body comes back. This is visible with `boot: false`; with `boot: true` the body flicker is at opacity 0 on that frame and hides it.

The fixer disclosed that entrances no longer replay, but not that they are never seen for a panel that starts collapsed, nor the stale frame.

problems.title: Fix 203: a name made only of empty strings still gives the panel a heading, labelled with a blank
problems.explanation: `named` is `name.isNotEmpty`, and `name` joins the non-null parts with spaces. Two or more empty strings (`code: ''`, `cjk: ''`, as a data-bound panel passes before its data arrives) give ' ', so the band becomes a heading node whose label is one space and the code block and title are excluded. The comment above says a panel with no name has no heading. The old code had the same weakness (`label.isEmpty`); the fix rewrote this code without closing it.
